Operational next step: Show a clear decline; suggest a supported alternate method; do not retry repeatedly without reason
Avoid: Do not label every decline as provider downtime
Evidence to capture: Timestamp, transaction reference, response code/category, masked method

Operational next step: Query the provider/acquirer status API or dashboard; reconcile against transaction ID; show pending until outcome is known
Avoid: Do not create a new charge just because the first response timed out
Evidence to capture: Order ID, payment ID, idempotency key, request/response timestamps, webhook events

Scenario: UPI payer debited but beneficiary not credited
Operational next step: Check status and bank/reference details; track reversal window under applicable RBI/NPCI rules; provide realistic status updates
Avoid: Do not assume debit alone means merchant success
Evidence to capture: UPI transaction ID, RRN/UTR if available, payer/beneficiary bank status, timestamps
Reference: NPCI UPI FAQs; RBI failed transaction TAT circular

Customer-visible symptom: Bank/app appears successful but order remains unpaid
Operational next step: Reconcile provider status; process webhook idempotently; repair order state and send a confirmation once authoritative status is known
Avoid: Do not mark order paid from a browser redirect alone
Evidence to capture: Order ID, payment ID, webhook event ID, signature validation result, event timestamps

Customer-visible symptom: Authorized payment not reflected as expected in reports
Operational next step: Compare authorization, capture, settlement, fee and payout reports; open a provider ticket with row-level evidence
Avoid: Do not compare totals from different time zones/cut-off windows without normalizing
Evidence to capture: Payment/capture IDs, batch, amount, currency, fees, settlement date

Customer-visible symptom: Refund initiated but bank statement has not updated
Operational next step: Check refund status, initiation timestamp, reference ID, rail/provider SLA; explain that refund processing and issuer posting are different steps
Avoid: Do not promise an exact credit time without product/bank policy
Evidence to capture: Original payment ID, refund ID, amount, initiation time, current state

Customer-visible symptom: Card cannot be added or wallet payment fails before checkout
Operational next step: Check issuer and wallet eligibility, device/account state, token status and provider/network support; escalate with non-sensitive codes
Avoid: Never ask for full card details or security code in support chat
Evidence to capture: Masked token reference, device/platform version, timestamp, error category
Reference: Google Pay tokenization help; Apple Pay planning

Operational next step: Compare payment IDs, order IDs, amount/time, idempotency key; identify duplicate vs authorization hold; follow provider procedure
Avoid: Do not trigger another payment while checking
Evidence to capture: Both transaction IDs, order ID, times, status, request idempotency key

Scenario: Fraud/dispute or cardholder says “I did not make this”
Operational next step: Follow issuer/acquirer/provider dispute path, preserve logs, meet evidence deadlines and escalate to the fraud team
Avoid: Do not frame a dispute as a routine refund or share another party’s data
Evidence to capture: Dispute case ID, transaction identifiers, evidence deadline, authorized records
Reference: Mastercard merchant rules and chargeback guide
